defects: Long static holds: the bergamot and black-tea pairs are nearly identical 1/6 s apart. Only a slight rotation or drift, so these shots read as posters on a timer, not animation.
Shots are cut on a mechanical 2.5 s grid (median 2.5 s, longest 5.0 s), and 4 of 14 seconds barely change from the previous second.
The 'All in one cup.' line-mask reveal leaves the second line cut off at its baseline. The frame looks unfinished mid-move, and it is a plain rise-in with no overshoot or settle.
The leaf in the black-tea cup appears in one sample and is gone in the pair, so it looks like a pop or a hard toggle rather than a staged action.
The cups' swirl and steam are just slow looping drift. The liquid has no weight, no pour and no surface reaction.

End card: the small 'Washed · single origin' text and the condensed type on the 'Out Friday' pill are tight and low-contrast at delivery size. Three type voices (condensed grotesk, sans, serif logo) compete on one frame.
Transitions between shots aren't visible in the samples. They look like straight colour-field cuts or wipes, not handoffs built on the circle motif.
gaps: Choreography: the circle motif (sun, bergamot, peach, cup) is the obvious match-cut device but never carries motion. Each circle should morph or roll into the next and finally drop into the cup, so the shots chain together instead of sitting as separate posters.

Timing and energy: there is no build. Holds sit at even lengths and the busiest moments come around 50-65%, then the piece drifts into the end card. Top work tightens the shots to about 1-1.5 s, speeds up into a peak around 70%, and then releases with a real settle.

Sound to picture: the track sounds like produced music with stutter dropouts at about 2.6, 7.6 and 12.3 s, but there is no visible sound design for objects (slice, leaf, pour, clink). The picture isn't driven by the audio's transients; it just sits on the bar grid. The roughly 0.4 s silence before the end card isn't used visually.
